skill.name: project-checklist
skill.description: プロジェクトの設計で検討すべき事項が充足しているかを、実物で確認して判定する。masseater/typescript-template から作ったリポジトリでは、GitHub の設定とテンプレートへの移行も扱う。新しいリポジトリの作成時、AI に移行を任せたあと、大きな変更の前、既存のプロジェクトの見直しで使う。
skill.summary: Review project readiness with evidence-based checklists and assess TypeScript template migrations and GitHub settings.
skill.author: masseater

security_audit.summary: All 44 static findings are false positives involving Markdown formatting, readable Japanese text, example configuration, or legitimate GitHub commands. Two semantic risks remain: repository changes during assessment and guidance that omits pre-merge verification. No evidence found of credential exfiltration, obfuscated payloads, or prompt injection.

remediation.issue: The assessment workflow invokes setup and changes repository settings despite its stated assessment-only boundary.
remediation.suggestion: Make checks read-only by default. Require separate approval for setup, display configuration differences, and preserve existing rules and secrets.

remediation.issue: Template guidance requires verification only after merging and treats pre-merge verification as obsolete.
remediation.suggestion: Run verification on pull requests or merge queues and require successful checks before merging. Preserve existing review and security requirements.

semantic_findings.title: Assessment Workflow Changes Repository Configuration
semantic_findings.description: The check workflow instructs execution of setup during assessment, despite the assessment-only rule. Setup uploads secrets, changes Actions permissions, enables auto-merge, and replaces a named ruleset without a separate approval step. This can change repository security controls during a requested review.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The check workflow explicitly requires setup through its confirmation stage. Setup contains mutating GitHub API calls and ruleset replacement, with no separate approval requirement.

semantic_findings.title: Template Criteria Omit Pre-Merge Verification
semantic_findings.description: Template criteria require verify only on main pushes or manual runs and treat pull-request verification as obsolete. Setup requires only the up-to-date status check. Changes can therefore reach the default branch before tests and security checks run, even when deployment remains gated.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The criteria explicitly exclude PR verification and assume no per-PR review. The shown ruleset requires only up-to-date, not successful verification before merge.

content.value_statement: Passing builds can hide missing design decisions and operational safeguards. This skill guides evidence-based project reviews and checks TypeScript template migrations and GitHub configuration.
actual_capabilities: Classifies checklist items as satisfied, deficient, unverified, or not applicable, with supporting evidence.
Reviews 16 general areas, including access control, privacy, delivery, performance, accessibility, and operational cost.
Compares production behavior, build outputs, repository files, and project-specific acceptance criteria.
Checks TypeScript template components for installation, functioning integration, and obsolete configuration.
Provides GitHub CLI setup steps for repository secrets, Actions permissions, auto-merge, and default-branch rules.
Produces an assessment table followed by separate lists of deficiencies and unverified items.
limitations: This is an instruction-based checklist, not a bundled scanner or a guarantee of security or compliance.
Production measurements require authorized access and external tools; unavailable evidence remains unverified.
Template checks assume the masseater TypeScript template, Vite+, and related tooling; some guidance references separately available skills.
The check workflow invokes setup mutations, and template guidance omits pre-merge verification; both need explicit review before use.

use_cases.title: Assess Release Readiness
use_cases.description: Review access controls, deployment paths, monitoring, recovery, and production evidence before a release.

use_cases.title: Review Template Migration Completeness
use_cases.description: Compare a migrated repository against template components and identify missing hooks, disconnected checks, or obsolete configuration.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Existing Project Decisions
use_cases.description: Collect evidence for cost, privacy, performance, accessibility, and published resources when planning a substantial project change.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Repository Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this repository with project-checklist. Keep the assessment read-only. List deficiencies and unverified items, and cite evidence for each judgment.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Without Production Access
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this project using repository files and build outputs only. Mark production-dependent items unverified and explain the missing evidence. Do not change settings.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Template Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare this repository with the masseater TypeScript template. Check installation, functioning integration, and obsolete configuration. Report differences before running commands or applying setup changes.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Controlled GitHub Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a GitHub setup plan for the selected repository. Preserve existing protections and require pre-merge verification. Show proposed changes and await approval before executing mutations.

output_examples.input: Review a repository that has no production deployment.
output: Requirements: satisfied. The project documentation identifies intended users and supported tasks.
Production performance: unverified. No production URL is available.
Deficiencies and unverified items: collect production measurements after deployment.

output_examples.input: Assess a template migration without applying fixes.
output: Verification entry point: satisfied. The repository provides a shared verification command.
Hook integration: deficient. The configured hook directory does not match the installed hooks.
GitHub settings: unverified. Administrative API access is unavailable.

best_practices: Specify the target repository, authorized production URLs, and read-only boundaries before starting.
Require observed evidence for each judgment and keep unavailable checks explicitly unverified.
Approve setup separately, enter secrets outside chat, and preserve existing review and pre-merge security checks.
anti_patterns: Treating written configuration or passing builds as proof that production safeguards work.
Allowing a checklist review to replace branch protections or change secrets without explicit approval.
Removing pre-merge verification or weakening checks merely to match template preferences.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The skill supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Command execution also requires the relevant local tools and permissions.

faq.question: What does a review produce?
faq.answer: It produces a table of areas, items, current conditions, judgments, and evidence. Separate lists identify deficient and unverified items.

faq.question: Can I use it without production access?
faq.answer: Yes. Repository and build checks remain possible, but production-dependent checks must be marked unverified.

faq.question: Does the assessment change my repository?
faq.answer: The main instructions prohibit assessment-time fixes, but the template check invokes setup changes. Request read-only operation and approve setup separately.

faq.question: How are credentials handled?
faq.answer: Setup uses GitHub CLI to store user-provided repository secrets. Enter values through the CLI rather than sharing them in chat.

faq.question: Does the checklist certify security?
faq.answer: No. It guides evidence collection rather than certification. Review its GitHub mutations and post-merge verification guidance before adopting template settings.
